subject: Onboarding certification checkpoint: load/pass criteria and artifact handoff
messages:
From: Jordan Reyes <jordan@blueharbor.ai>
To: Ethan Park <ethan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 6 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Onboarding next steps — load validation scope

Thanks Ethan — great call today. As discussed, our primary goal for the certification window is to validate that Redwood meets our 99th‑percentile latency SLO of 220ms for 512 token chat inference and sustained throughput for 1k RPS over 10 minutes at our peak mix.

I attached the load-plan spreadsheet with our traffic mix and token distributions. Can you confirm a recommended run order (warmup, steady, spike) and what telemetry you need from us for post-run analysis?

Samira and I are available for the run on Thu (9/9) morning PT.

—Jordan


-----Original Message-----
From: Ethan Park <ethan@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Reyes <jordan@blueharbor.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 6 Sep 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Onboarding next steps — load validation scope

Jordan — thanks for the file, that helps. Quick answers up front:
- Recommended run: 15m warmup (gradual ramp to 60% peak), 10m steady at peak mix, 3x 60s spikes to 150% peak, and a 10m cooldown.
- Telemetry: per‑request latency histograms (p50/p95/p99), token counts, throughput (RPS), GPU utilization, host CPU, and KV‑cache hit rates. Please include a sample of full request+response traces for any tail‑latency outliers.

I've attached our acceptance checklist and will deploy a dedicated test pool (q4‑small) for the run. Monica — can you pick an arrival window for the run? Ben — engineering will capture kernel metrics and KV cache stats; I'll need an ssh key for access to the run logs bucket.

Thanks,
Ethan


From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Reyes <jordan@blueharbor.ai>, Ethan Park <ethan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Onboarding next steps — load validation scope

Jordan — Thu 9/9 09:30–10:30 PT works on our side. I will be monitoring the run and coordinating roll‑forwards if we hit preconfigured thresholds.

Checklist highlights I'll validate live:
- Canary traffic routing verified
- KV cache primed (3 repop cycles)
- Autoscaler policy pinned for test pool
- Inflight log stream to shared Drive folder

Jordan/Samira — please upload your test SSH key to the Drive folder before 9/9 so Ben can grant read access to logs.

Monica


From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Reyes <jordan@blueharbor.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ethan Park <ethan@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 9 Sep 2026 11:58:00 -07:00
Subject: Run results: 2026‑09‑09 09:30 PT — initial pass

Team — quick summary from the run we completed this morning (artifacts attached):
- Steady 10m at 1k RPS: p50=48ms, p95=162ms, p99=204ms (all <220ms target).
- 3x 60s spikes (to 1.5k RPS): observed increased p99 to 276ms during first spike; subsequent two spikes had p99 at 232ms and 218ms.
- KV cache hit rate: 88% on average during steady; drop to 61% during first spike.
- GPU util: avg 67% steady, spike to 92% on first burst.

Attachments included: load_results_0909.csv (tokenized request samples + latency), kv_cache_snapshot_0909.tar.gz (primed keys snapshot), raw_trace_samples.txt.

Notes / next actions:
1) Engineering (Ben) to rerun a focused spike test with cache warmup change (increase priming to 5 cycles) to see if first‑spike tail improves.
2) Monica/Ethan to review autoscaler cooldown settings — current cooldown extended to 45s which may delay scale during sudden bursts.
3) Jordan/Samira to review downstream client retry/backoff behavior for negative impact on spikes.

I'll schedule the focused rerun for Fri 9/10 morning.

—Ben


From: Jordan Reyes <jordan@blueharbor.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ethan Park <ethan@redwood.ai>, Samira Khatri <samira@blueharbor.ai>
Date: Thu, 9 Sep 2026 12:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Run results: 2026‑09‑09 09:30 PT — initial pass

Appreciate the readout — overall promising. The early spike behavior is our main concern (it amplifies downstream retries). We'll do the following on our side:
- Add jitter to client retries and reduce default retry attempts in the SDK for spike windows.
- Provide a second request sample set that skews longer dialogs to test token pressure.

Please send the updated run invitation for Fri when Ben has the rerun slot. Also confirm whether Redwood will consider pinning a slightly larger test pool for the second run to avoid autoscale lag affecting p99.

—Jordan


From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Reyes <jordan@blueharbor.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Ethan Park <ethan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 10 Sep 2026 07:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Follow up: focused spike rerun scheduled + artifacts

Jordan — rerun scheduled for Fri 9/10 09:00 PT. For this run we pinned two additional instances to the test pool (temporary) and increased KV priming to 5 cycles. Attached are the run invite and the small checklist; I'll pull live traces and upload artifacts to the Drive folder after the run.

Expected deliverables after rerun:
- Updated CSV of per‑request latencies (same columns as previous)
- Comparative p99 delta report (baseline vs. rerun)
- Trace samples for top 10 tail requests

Lauren will be handling the final evidence package for SOC ingestion.

—Ben


From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Reyes <jordan@blueharbor.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ethan Park <ethan@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>, Samira Khatri <samira@blueharbor.ai>
Date: Mon, 13 Sep 2026 16:04:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Run results: 2026‑09‑09 09:30 PT — initial pass / certification status

Jordan/Samira — follow up from the focused rerun:
- Focused spike rerun (9/10) results: p99 during spike improved from 276ms -> 216ms with 5 priming cycles and the pinned extra instances. Steady state metrics unchanged.
- Artifact bundle uploaded to Drive: load_results_0909.csv, load_results_0910.csv, kv_cache_snapshot_0909.tar.gz, rerun_trace_samples.txt, acceptance-checklist-ethan.docx.
- Temp pool removed after testing; production pool unchanged.

Conclusion: BlueHarbor passes the Redwood onboarding certification for the defined targets (99th <=220ms for 512 tokens; 1k RPS steady). There are operational notes regarding autoscaler cooldown and client retry behavior which we recommend tracking in the go‑live runbook.

Next steps:
1) Ethan/Ben to add autoscaler cooldown recommendation to the runbook (PR by 9/17).
2) Jordan to confirm go‑live date and whether BlueHarbor wants Redwood to run a pre‑production five‑minute burst test on day‑one.
3) Lauren to prepare final evidence packet for SOC ingestion and hand it to the customer success folder.

Thanks everyone — nice cross‑team work.

Monica

--
Monica Patel
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
"Helping customers validate predictable inference"
